g.text: What’s it like? Having the freedom to swan about in a city filled with plague and know you’ll never have to worry about catching it?
I don’t know I won’t catch it. I just haven’t yet.
It’s fantastic. I can help the people in danger.
I’ll speak as I like, thank you very much.
Heh. That was Entrati’s whole schtick. Back when he first appeared with the whole ‘Doktor Friday’ medicine show bit.
And I’ll tell you when you’re out of line.
I’ve seen how you work. You might have been human once, but now you’re Spanglyboots the Space Elf. All spooky light shows and mystic powers.
I don’t think you can be killed. Not forever. And I know how hard people have tried.
Makes one wonder why he never got infected. His family did, after all.
He managed to protect himself from succumbing, at least. Maybe he’s more like you than you know.
You don’t act scared of the Techrot. Why should you? You have no reason to be.
Höllvania’s had a whole bunch of would-be saviours.
Eleanor’s being a bitter lemon today.
You’re not going to catch it.
The Princess, back in the day. Then Entrati. Viktor. My brother, of course. Now you.
Sol, I miss the taste of lemons.
You don’t know this thing like I do. It evolves. It mutates. It learns. The Orokin thought they could beat it. They never did.
Maybe you’re right. But we don’t KNOW.
You’re right. I could help people more.
Do you see yourself as a hero?
Oh Gods, I remember now. Eris. The hulks. The surface of Deimos.
I keep forgetting we don’t win against the Techrot.
I suppose not. And I have no business speculating, really.
Nothing I’d be proud to admit to.
It makes what we’re trying to do here feel pointless, almost.
It just galls me to see you so above it all, you know?
I simply cannot understand how you were trapped in a storybook kingdom and STILL haven’t outgrown that sort of thing.
But thanks for checking in, regardless.
Sol. Here I am feeling sorry for myself for being a plague victim, and dumping on you for being immune, and you’ve seen whole worlds get eaten by the selfsame poxy crud.
Ignore me. Oozing blemishes are ugly enough. Self-pity is uglier.
I’m glad. Someone who’s lived as many centuries as you have OUGHT to be a grown-up by now.
Good for you. Because I’ve seen what happened when one little boy thought he’d go off on a Hero’s Journey and started thinking of the rest of us as his supporting characters.
I think I’ll count what blessings I have.
